title: Lifting a formally smooth complete local algebra along a finite residually trivial map
statement: Let $\alpha:(A_0,\mathfrak m_0)\to(A,\mathfrak m_A)$ be a local homomorphism of Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local rings which are complete ($\mathfrak m_0$-adically, resp. $\mathfrak m_A$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]), such that $A$ is a finitely generated $A_0$-module via $\alpha$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $\alpha$ induces an isomorphism of residue fields $A_0/\mathfrak m_0\xrightarrow{\sim}A/\mathfrak m_A=:k$. Let $\varphi:A\to(B,\mathfrak m_B)$ be a flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] local homomorphism into a Noetherian local ring which is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete, such that the closed fibre $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is formally smooth over $k$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic], $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$. Then there exist a Noetherian local ring $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ which is $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, a local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ such that $C$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology, and a local homomorphism $\psi:C\to B$ with $\psi\circ\gamma=\varphi\circ\alpha$, such that the ring map $C\otimes_{A_0}A\to B$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $c\otimes a\mapsto\psi(c)\varphi(a)$, is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (remark-what-does-it-mean, line 10308), parts (3) and (4), with Lemma Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs, line 10256) and Lemma 07NJ (lift-continuous); as used in the proof of Proposition 07PM (fs-regular, line 12028), second paragraph, where 'completion in the tensor product is not needed as A_0 -> A is finite' by Algebra Lemma 00MA (completion-tensor). Formal smoothness of A_0 -> C in the source is Definition 07NI with A_0 m_0-adic; for a local homomorphism it is the condition of def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic (Lemma 07EC(2))

proof.text: *The closed fibre.* As $\varphi$ is local, $\mathfrak m_AB\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$ is a proper ideal, so by [lem-weil-pbc-complete-local-quotient] $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ is a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}=\mathfrak m_B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and is $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $\pi:B\to\overline B$ be the quotient map. Since $\pi\varphi$ kills $\mathfrak m_A$, $\overline B$ is a $k$-algebra, and through the residue isomorphism $\bar\alpha:k_0=A_0/\mathfrak m_0\xrightarrow{\sim}k$ a $k_0$-algebra; the composite $A_0\to k_0\to k\to\overline B$ is $\pi\varphi\alpha$. A homomorphism of $k$-algebras is the same as a homomorphism of $k_0$-algebras for the structure through the isomorphism $\bar\alpha$, so the lifting condition of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $k\to\overline B$ (hypothesis) is the one for $k_0\to\overline B$: $\overline B$ is formally smooth over $k_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (remark-what-does-it-mean, line 10308): 'pick A -> C as in Lemma 07NR lifting B (x)_{A'} k over k'; Algebra, Lemma Tag 0325 (lemma-quotient-complete-local) for the closed fibre

proof.text: *The lift $C$ of $\overline B$.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-from-residue-field] to $A_0$ and $E=\overline B$ with $k_0\to\overline B$ from Step 1: there are a Noetherian local ring $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$, $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, a local homomorphism $\gamma:A_0\to C$ with $C$ formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology, and an isomorphism of $A_0$-algebras $\sigma:C/\mathfrak m_0C\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline B$. Let $p:C\to C/\mathfrak m_0C$ be the quotient map and $\theta=\sigma p:C\to\overline B$, a surjective homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras: $\theta\gamma=\pi\varphi\alpha$, with kernel $\mathfrak m_0C$. Since $\gamma$ is local, $\mathfrak m_0C\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$, so $\mathfrak m_C/\mathfrak m_0C$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring $C/\mathfrak m_0C$, which the ring isomorphism $\sigma$ maps onto the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$; hence $\theta(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_{\overline B}$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308), first paragraph, applying Lemma Tag 07NR (lemma-lift-fs, line 10256)

proof.text: *The map $\psi:C\to B$.* Regard $B$ as an $A_0$-algebra through $\varphi\alpha$; then $\overline B=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ with the quotient map $\pi$ is an $A_0$-algebra through $\pi\varphi\alpha$, and $\theta$ is a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras (Step 2). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete] with $R=A_0$, $S=C$, $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_C$, the $R$-algebra $B$, $I=\mathfrak m_B$, $J=\mathfrak m_AB$, $t=1$, $q=\pi$, $g=\theta$, $r=1$. Its hypotheses hold: $C$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology (Step 2); $B$ is $\mathfrak m_B$-adically complete (hypothesis); $J^1\subseteq I$ as $\varphi$ is local; $J=\bigcap_m(J+\mathfrak m_B^m)$, because $(J+\mathfrak m_B^m)/J=\mathfrak m_B^m(B/J)$ and $\bigcap_m\mathfrak m_B^m(B/J)=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] for the Noetherian ring $B$, the ideal $\mathfrak m_B$ (the Jacobson radical of the local ring $B$) and the finitely generated $B$-module $B/J$; and $\theta(\mathfrak m_C)=\mathfrak m_{\overline B}=\pi(\mathfrak m_B)=q(I)$ (Step 2). It gives a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras $\psi:C\to B$ with $\pi\psi=\theta$; being a homomorphism of $A_0$-algebras means $\psi\gamma=\varphi\alpha$. $\psi$ is local: $\psi(\mathfrak m_C)\subseteq\pi^{-1}(\theta(\mathfrak m_C))=\pi^{-1}(\mathfrak m_{\overline B})=\mathfrak m_B$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308): 'By formal smoothness we can find the arrow C -> B, see Lemma 07NJ' (lemma-lift-continuous, line 9257)

proof.text: *A power of $\mathfrak m_A$ lies in $\mathfrak m_0A$.* Let $\mathfrak m_0A$ be the ideal of $A$ generated by $\alpha(\mathfrak m_0)$; $\mathfrak m_0A\subseteq\mathfrak m_A$ as $\alpha$ is local. $\overline A=A/\mathfrak m_0A$ is a finitely generated module over $A_0/\mathfrak m_0=k_0$ (images of $A_0$-module generators of $A$), i.e. a finite-dimensional $k_0$-vector space, and its ideals are $k_0$-subspaces (as $A_0$ acts through $\alpha$); so every descending chain of ideals of $\overline A$ is eventually constant, and $\overline A$, a quotient of the local ring $A$ by a proper ideal, is an Artinian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_0A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent] $(\mathfrak m_A/\mathfrak m_0A)^N=0$ for some $N\ge1$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_A^N\subseteq\mathfrak m_0A$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308), part (3) ('if A -> A' is finite') and Proposition Tag 07PM (proposition-fs-regular, line 12028), second paragraph ('A_0 -> A is finite'); the nilpotence is written out here

proof.text: *The ring $D=C\otimes_{A_0}A$ and the map $\Phi$.* Let $D=C\otimes_{A_0}A$ [def-weil-module-base-change], $C$ an $A_0$-algebra by $\gamma$ and $A$ by $\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property] $D$ is a commutative ring with ring maps $\iota_C:c\mapsto c\otimes1$, $\iota_A:a\mapsto1\otimes a$, and since $\psi$ and $\varphi$ are homomorphisms of $A_0$-algebras into $B$ ($\psi\gamma=\varphi\alpha$, Step 3) there is a ring homomorphism $\Phi:D\to B$ with $\Phi(c\otimes a)=\psi(c)\varphi(a)$: the map of the statement. Let $a_1,\dots,a_r$ generate $A$ as an $A_0$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; for $a=\sum_j\alpha(x_j)a_j$ we get $c\otimes a=\sum_j\gamma(x_j)c\otimes a_j=\sum_j\iota_C(\gamma(x_j)c)\,(1\otimes a_j)$, so $D$ is generated as a $C$-module (through $\iota_C$) by $1\otimes a_1,\dots,1\otimes a_r$, and $\Phi(D)=\sum_j\psi(C)\varphi(a_j)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] $D$ is a Noetherian ring, and by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical] applied to the local ring $C$ the ideal $\mathfrak m_CD$ is contained in every maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$ of $D$. For $a\in\mathfrak m_A$, Step 4 gives $\iota_A(a)^N=\iota_A(a^N)\in\iota_A(\mathfrak m_0A)D$, and $\iota_A(\alpha(x))=1\otimes\alpha(x)=\gamma(x)\otimes1=\iota_C(\gamma(x))\in\mathfrak m_CD$ for $x\in\mathfrak m_0$; so $\iota_A(a)^N\in\mathfrak M$ and, $\mathfrak M$ being prime, $\iota_A(a)\in\mathfrak M$. Hence the ideal $\mathfrak m_AD$ generated by $\iota_A(\mathfrak m_A)$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $D$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308), the map C (x)_A A' -> B, and Proposition Tag 07PM (line 12028), second paragraph: 'Completion in the tensor product is not needed as A_0 -> A is finite' (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00MA); the finiteness of D over C is what is used here

proof.text: *$\Phi$ is surjective.* View $B$ as a $C$-module through $\psi$; for an ideal $\mathfrak a$ of $C$ write $\mathfrak aB$ for the ideal generated by $\psi(\mathfrak a)$, and $\mathfrak m_AB$, $\mathfrak m_0B$ for those generated by $\varphi(\mathfrak m_A)$, $\varphi\alpha(\mathfrak m_0)$. Since $\pi\psi=\theta$ is surjective, $B=\psi(C)+\mathfrak m_AB$. Hence for $x\in\mathfrak m_A^i$ and $b=\psi(c)+b'$ with $b'\in\mathfrak m_AB$ we have $\varphi(x)b=\varphi(x)\psi(c)+\varphi(x)b'\in\Phi(D)+\mathfrak m_A^{i+1}B$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_A^iB\subseteq\Phi(D)+\mathfrak m_A^{i+1}B$ ($\Phi(D)$ is a subring of $B$ containing $\varphi(A)\psi(C)$), and by induction on $i$, $B\subseteq\Phi(D)+\mathfrak m_A^NB$. By Step 4, $\mathfrak m_A^NB\subseteq\mathfrak m_0B$, and $\mathfrak m_0B$, the ideal generated by $\varphi\alpha(\mathfrak m_0)=\psi\gamma(\mathfrak m_0)\subseteq\psi(\mathfrak m_C)$, is contained in $\mathfrak m_CB$. So $B=\sum_j\psi(C)\varphi(a_j)+\mathfrak m_CB$ (Step 5): the images of $\varphi(a_1),\dots,\varphi(a_r)$ generate $B/\mathfrak m_CB$ over $C/\mathfrak m_C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-complete-ring] to the ring $C$, the ideal $\mathfrak m_C$ and the $C$-module $B$: (1) $C$ is $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete (Step 2); (2) $\bigcap_n\mathfrak m_C^nB\subseteq\bigcap_n\mathfrak m_B^n=0$, as $\psi(\mathfrak m_C)\subseteq\mathfrak m_B$ (Step 3) and by [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] for the Noetherian ring $B$, its Jacobson radical $\mathfrak m_B$ and $M=B$; (3) $B/\mathfrak m_CB$ is finitely generated over $C/\mathfrak m_C$. It gives that $\varphi(a_1),\dots,\varphi(a_r)$ generate $B$ as a $C$-module, so $B=\sum_j\psi(C)\varphi(a_j)=\Phi(D)$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308), proof of (1) and (3) (Nakayama's lemma, Algebra Lemma Tag 00DV, for C (x)_A A'/m^n -> B/m^nB); here, D being finite over C, the surjectivity is obtained at once from Algebra, Lemma Tag 031D (lemma-finite-over-complete-ring, line 22860) instead of through the completion

proof.text: *$\Phi$ is injective.* Let $K=\ker\Phi$, an ideal of $D$. Regard $D$ as an $A$-module through $\iota_A$ and $B$ through $\varphi$; $\Phi$ is $A$-linear ($\Phi\iota_A=\varphi$), so $0\to K\to D\xrightarrow{\Phi}B\to0$ is a short exact sequence of $A$-modules (Step 6), and $B$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] by hypothesis. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] with $N=k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, the sequence $0\to K/\mathfrak m_AK\to D/\mathfrak m_AD\to B/\mathfrak m_AB\to0$ is exact (for an $A$-module $P$, $P\otimes_Ak=P/\mathfrak m_AP$). The map $\bar\Phi:D/\mathfrak m_AD\to\overline B$ is injective: as $A=\alpha(A_0)+\mathfrak m_A$ ($\bar\alpha$ is onto), $c\otimes a\equiv c\otimes\alpha(x)=\gamma(x)c\otimes1\pmod{\mathfrak m_AD}$, so every class is that of some $c\otimes1$; if $\bar\Phi(c\otimes1)=\pi\psi(c)=\theta(c)=0$ then $c\in\mathfrak m_0C$ (Step 2), $c=\sum\gamma(x_i)c_i$ with $x_i\in\mathfrak m_0$, and $c\otimes1=\sum c_i\otimes\alpha(x_i)\in\mathfrak m_AD$. Hence $K/\mathfrak m_AK=0$, i.e. $K=(\mathfrak m_AD)K$. $K$ is a finitely generated $D$-module ($D$ Noetherian, Step 5) and $\mathfrak m_AD$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $D$ (Step 5), so $K=0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-jacobson].

source.place: More on Algebra, Remark Tag 07NS (line 10308), part (4) ('if A' -> B is flat, then C (x)^_A A' = B'), argued as in the proof of Proposition Tag 07NQ (proposition-fs-flat-fibre-fs, line 10081): 'tensoring the short exact sequence 0 -> I -> S (x)_R A -> B -> 0 over A with k we find I (x)_A k = 0 hence I = 0 by Nakayama' (Algebra, Lemma Tag 00HL for the exactness, Lemma Tag 00DV for Nakayama)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ is a Noetherian local ring, $\mathfrak m_C$-adically complete, $\gamma:A_0\to C$ is local and $C$ is formally smooth over $A_0$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology (Step 2); $\psi:C\to B$ is local with $\psi\gamma=\varphi\alpha$ (Step 3); and the ring homomorphism $\Phi:C\otimes_{A_0}A\to B$, $c\otimes a\mapsto\psi(c)\varphi(a)$ (Step 5), is bijective (Steps 6 and 7), hence an isomorphism of rings.

Proof written in 8 steps: closed fibre complete (0325 node); lift C of the closed fibre by 07NR (new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-from-residue-field, isomorphism stated as one of A_0-algebras, as the source's proof gives); the map psi by 07NJ (existing node lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-lift-into-complete, closedness of m_A B by Krull); m_A^N in m_0 A (Artinian quotient); D = C (x)_{A_0} A finite over C, Noetherian, m_A D in the Jacobson radical; surjectivity of D -> B by 031D (in place of the source's Nakayama mod m^n plus completion, which the finite case makes unnecessary, as 07PM remarks); injectivity by tensoring the kernel sequence with k (B flat, 00HL) and Nakayama, as in the proof of 07NQ; conclusion.
